html:
Kim Jong Un has ruled North Korea since the death of his father Kim Jong Il in December 2011, the third of his family to lead the state. He was born in about 1984 and partly schooled in Switzerland.

He secured power by purging and executing rivals, among them his uncle Jang Song-thaek in 2013; his half brother Kim Jong-nam was murdered with a nerve agent at Kuala Lumpur airport in 2017. He sped up the weapons programme begun by his father, testing a thermonuclear device and missiles able to reach the United States in 2017.

He then met Donald Trump in Singapore in 2018 and at Panmunjom in 2019, without a deal. Since 2023 he has drawn close to Russia, sending shells and later troops for its war in Ukraine. His grandfather Kim Il Sung remains the state's eternal president.
